properties.rationale: Deferred on the established disposition for this review, 2026-07-28. Accepted and not dropped; like the correspondence requirement it comes from general architecture and risk practice rather than from reflow, which had no equivalent either. Deferred because the modelling choice is unsettled and cheap-versus-honest pull in opposite directions: a new node type keeps the distinction sharp (an assumption is not enforced like a Constraint, not chosen like a Decision, and not reducible like a Risk), while adding a kind to Constraint is cheaper and risks blurring the very difference that makes it useful. Also undecided: what edge carries "rests on", and whether an assumption carries a confirmation cadence — cap:freshness already models when a claim was last confirmed, so "nobody has checked this in six months" could be computed rather than remembered. The computation matters more than the node: once assumptions have things hanging off them, "X no longer holds" becomes a propagate query with a real answer instead of prose inside a Decision rationale that nothing can walk.
